project.title: A full revenue stack for a made‑up B2B software company
project.sentence: One lead followed the whole way: ad click, consent, form, CRM, routing, conversions sent back to the ad platform, and the report at the end. Built in six parts on a made-up company, Roadwren, so all of it can be public.
project.built_with: Next.js, Tag Manager, GA4, HubSpot, Salesforce Flow, Python, SQL, dbt
project.own: I designed the whole system and I am building every part of it myself: the tracked site, the lead routing, the scoring, the cleanup and the reporting. The company, Roadwren, is made up, so every file is public.

journey.name: The page gets checked
journey.gets: A landing page that is about to go live
journey.hands_on: A page that passed its checks
journey.why: Everything after this depends on the tag firing. One bad page and the leads from it never get counted.

journey.name: The visit is tracked, if the visitor agrees
journey.gets: A visitor who clicked an ad
journey.hands_on: The form fill, the click ID and consent
journey.why: Without the click ID, nobody later on can say which ad this lead came from.

journey.name: The lead gets an owner
journey.gets: The form fill, with the click ID still attached
journey.hands_on: A lead with a stage, a campaign and an owner
journey.why: A lead nobody owns is a lead nobody calls. And the ad platform only learns if it hears which clicks became real leads.

journey.name: The lead gets read and scored
journey.hands_on: A scored lead, with the reasons
journey.why: Rules can sort by size. They cannot read a lead. This does, and it asks a person when it is unsure.

journey.name: Duplicates get merged
journey.hands_on: One record per person and company
journey.why: The same person entered twice gets counted twice in every report after this.

journey.name: It all gets added up
journey.hands_on: The funnel, ad credit and a checked report
journey.why: This is where a mistake anywhere earlier shows up. So the report refuses to publish a number it cannot prove.

choices: A visitor can say no to tracking.
Nothing is stored until they agree.
Click IDs wait in memory until consent. Browser storage is storage too.
Google and Meta match a sale to the most recent ad click.
A new ad click replaces the stored one.
Earlier touches are lost. That is the cost, and it is written down.
An unknown company size is not a small company.
Leads with no fleet size go to a review queue.
A wrong owner costs more than a short wait.
tldr: Most tracking setups lose the lead somewhere between the ad click and the report.
One lead followed the whole way, on a made-up company, in six parts.

builds.sentence: A demo site that stores a click ID only after consent and carries it through the form into the CRM.
builds.graded_on: With consent rejected: no cookie set, no click ID stored. With consent accepted: the click ID reaches the CRM.

image.alt: The Roadwren demo form with the cookie banner open, offering Reject all and Accept all, before any click ID is stored.
image.caption: The live demo form. The banner comes first: nothing is stored until Accept.

builds.card_title: A site that only tracks what the visitor agreed to

summary.did: Wrote the spec, built it with Claude Code, wrote the tests
problem: An ad platform needs a click ID to match a lead back to the ad.
Storing that ID before the visitor agrees breaks consent.
A marketing team has to prove both: consent is respected and the loop still closes.
built: All four consent signals start as denied, before any tag loads.
Click IDs wait in memory and are stored only after Accept.
The form carries them into HubSpot and fires one conversion event.
choices: Advanced consent mode over basic, so Google can still model rejected visits.
Last ad click over first, because that is the one a platform matches.
Memory, not browser storage, before consent. Browser storage is storage too.

builds.sentence: Leads from the form get a stage, a campaign and an owner in Salesforce. No lead is blocked. Conversions go back to Google Ads.
builds.graded_on: 37 test leads with an answer key: the right stage, reason, segment, channel, campaign and owner for each. Not run yet.
builds.card_title: Every lead gets an owner, and the sale goes back to Google Ads

summary.did: Wrote the rules and both answer keys, built the Flow by hand, saved the setup as files
problem: A lead with the wrong owner, or no owner, waits.
Ad platforms only learn which clicks became real leads if someone sends that back.
Routing built by clicking is hard to review and easy to break.
built: Every lead is saved. One that does not fit gets a stage and a reason.
Two Flows set the stage, the campaign and the owner queue from fleet size.
A script writes the Google Ads upload file and checks every row.
choices: Fleet size, not employee count. The price is per vehicle.
No lead is ever blocked. A blocked web lead is never created, so nobody can review it.
The setup is saved as files, so a change shows up as a diff.

builds.sentence: A Python tool that checks landing pages for tags, consent, the conversion event and UTM values before launch.
builds.graded_on: 14 pages with a planted bug and 8 clean pages: bugs caught, and false alarms raised.
builds.card_title: A checker that reads a landing page before the campaign launches

builds.sentence: Claude scores each new lead against a written rubric, routes the strong ones and asks a person when unsure.
builds.graded_on: Agreement with 36 hand labels, and whether a person's edit survives a second run.
builds.card_title: Leads scored against a written rubric, with the reasoning shown

builds.tile: Funnel in SQL and a reporting agent
builds.sentence: The funnel and ad credit in SQL, and a weekly summary where code checks every number before it is published.
builds.graded_on: Credit adds up to exactly 100 percent, and three planted wrong summaries are rejected.
builds.card_title: One funnel in SQL, and a report that refuses to publish a wrong number

builds.sentence: Duplicate accounts and contacts in Salesforce found and merged by script, with every merge graded.
builds.graded_on: Merges right and wrong against an answer key, with decoys that must be left alone.
builds.card_title: Duplicate records merged and checked against an answer key
